segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: My name is Sarah Meyer.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: I'm a pediatrician and the director of the Immunization Safety Office.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: Today I'll be sharing an update on CDC's COVID-19 vaccine safety monitoring.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: The goal of this presentation is to share with the committee how CDC monitors COVID-19 vaccine safety and what we have found through four and a half years of monitoring these vaccines.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: Before I get into the details, I want to state the bottom line up front.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: CDC and interagency partners launched an extensive vaccine safety monitoring program for COVID-19 vaccines.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: Many potential safety outcomes were rigorously assessed through complementary passive and active systems.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: Myocarditis has been causally associated with mRNA COVID-19 vaccines.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: In addition, adverse events common to all vaccines such as local and systemic reactions and allergic reactions have been observed.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: CDC continues to monitor the safety of COVID-19 vaccines.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: Vaccine safety monitoring is a key component of the entire vaccine life cycle.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: From the preclinical research and development to clinical trials and the reviews by regulatory agencies and advisory groups, safety is evaluated at every step.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: After a vaccine has been authorized or approved, CDC safety monitoring begins alongside our interagency partners.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: FDA, Indian Health Service, Department of Defense and Department of Veterans Affairs.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: CDC uses strong complementary systems in a layered approach to rapidly detect and assess potential safety concerns in order for public health officials and policymakers to take appropriate action.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: Most of these systems have been in place for decades, but we are continuing to improve the existing systems as well as identify new systems that are needed to fill gaps, such as V-safe, which was launched to monitor COVID-19 vaccines.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: Next, I will briefly describe each of these systems in more detail.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: I'll start with the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System, or VAERS.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: VAERS serves as our nation's early warning system for vaccine safety.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: This system is co-managed with FDA and involves nationwide spontaneous reporting to rapidly detect safety signals, including rare events.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: Healthcare providers and manufacturers are required under the National Childhood Vaccine Injury Act to submit VAERS reports for certain types of adverse events and vaccines.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: However, reports are encouraged from anyone, such as patients or their family member.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: An important point to stress is that a report to VAERS does not mean that a vaccine caused an adverse event.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: VAERS is used for signal detection and hypothesis generation and in most situations is not able to assess for causality.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: The Vaccine Safety Datalink or VSD is a collaborative model for generating high quality vaccine safety data.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: Thirteen integrated healthcare organizations participate in this network covering around 15 and a half million people per year.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: VSD involves active surveillance using electronic medical records and chart reviews.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: This allows for rapid monitoring for pre-specified events of interest, as well as for monitoring for unexpected events.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: As opposed to VAERS, which is used for signal detection, VSD can both detect as well as assess safety signals.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: Another hallmark of the VSD is the strong expertise in this network, which has allowed for the development of innovative methods for monitoring safety.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: The Clinical Immunization Safety Assessment or CISA project is a network to guide vaccine safety from the individual to the population level.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: The CISA project includes eight medical research centers with vaccine safety experts and subspecialists.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: CISA consultants provide individual clinical consultations on complex immunization issues to help guide patient care.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: CISA investigators also conduct clinical research on vaccine safety, geared towards real world issues not assessed in pre-licensure trials.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: Finally, CISA consultants help to inform CDC public health guidance on clinical immunization safety issues.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: Lastly, the V-safe after vaccination health checker is CDC's newest tool and involves direct to consumer vaccine safety monitoring.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: V-safe is a smartphone and computer-based self-reported active monitoring system established during the COVID-19 pandemic.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: It can serve as the earliest source of information on reactogenicity and other health events for new vaccines and in populations excluded from clinical trials.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: For example, V-SAFE provided a conduit to enroll more than 23,000 pregnant women into a voluntary registry to monitor maternal and neonatal outcomes after COVID-19 vaccination.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: Because it is flexible and able to be rapidly deployed, V-SAFE is an important tool for emergency preparedness and response.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: In addition, V-SAFE is integrated with VAERS to help streamline reporting of serious adverse events.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: These systems serve as the foundation for CDC's comprehensive approach to studying COVID-19 vaccine safety.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: This approach includes surveillance to analyze spontaneously reported events, epidemiologic studies to assess specific safety questions, clinical research to help guide clinical practice, a pregnancy registry for a longitudinal assessment of maternal and infant outcomes after COVID-19 vaccination,
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: Rapid cycle analyses to quickly detect potential concerns that require further investigation, data mining to assess for over 60,000 potential outcomes in order to detect unexpected events after vaccination, and patient surveys to assess symptoms and health impacts following vaccination.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: Through these analyses, we have not identified any new safety concerns outside of known events including myocarditis and pericarditis, allergic reactions, and common local and systemic reactions.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: So to summarize, we have identified several adverse events following mRNA COVID-19 vaccines.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: Most of these, including local and systemic reactions, acute allergic reactions, syncope and shoulder injuries can occur with any vaccine.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: Myocarditis and pericarditis have been observed following COVID-19 vaccination.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: We arrived at these conclusions by evaluating at least 65 specific safety outcomes, conducted data mining of at least 60,000 potential outcomes for unexpected concerns, investigated numerous statistical signals, and conducted many epidemiologic studies.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: Our findings are consistent with the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine in their consensus report on adverse effects of COVID-19 vaccines.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: This report was commissioned by HRSA and published in 2024.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: Over 400 studies on the safety of COVID-19 vaccines were reviewed as part of this evaluation.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: NASEM concluded that the evidence supported a causal association between mRNA COVID-19 vaccines and myocarditis, and that the evidence favors rejection of a causal relationship between vaccination and six additional outcomes, including Guillain-Barre syndrome, Bell's palsy, TTS, myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, and female infertility.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: The evidence was inadequate to accept or reject a causal relationship for 13 other outcomes.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: In summary, COVID-19 vaccines have been evaluated under the most extensive vaccine safety monitoring program in U.S. history.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: Safety surveillance rapidly identified and characterized the risk of myocarditis after mRNA COVID-19 vaccination.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: We identified no other confirmed safety concerns except those seen with any other vaccine such as local and systemic reactions or allergic reactions.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.text: CDC continues to prioritize the monitoring of COVID-19 vaccine safety with at least 30 ongoing studies or activities.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
